classification.difficultyReason: Recover class frequencies from cumulative totals, construct the corresponding histogram and identify the modal class.

inlines.text: The cumulative frequency histogram and polygon for a set of data is given below.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16, right column, graph below the stem
spec.description: Unshaded cumulative-frequency bars with a blue cumulative polygon, boundary labels 3–7 and cumulative-frequency labels 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
spec.mathematics: Bars on [3,4), [4,5), [5,6), [6,7) have cumulative heights 3, 4, 8, 10. The polygon joins (3,0), (4,3), (5,4), (6,8), (7,10).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied cumulative representation is visible; ordinary frequencies and the modal class are withheld.

inlines.text: Subtract consecutive cumulative frequencies to find each class frequency.
Each interval has width 1, so its histogram height equals its frequency.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16(a); checked against teacher PDF page 79, printed page 657
spec.description: Completed frequency histogram with four adjacent unshaded bars, horizontal boundary labels 3–7, vertical frequency ticks 1–4 and no frequency polygon.
spec.mathematics: Successive cumulative differences give frequencies 3, 1, 4, 2 for [3,4), [4,5), [5,6), [6,7). All class widths equal 1.

inlines.text: Find the mode of the data.

answer.worked: The highest frequency is $4$, in $[5,6)$. Therefore the modal class is $[5,6)$.
